data.function: P2 report: barrier pins for P5
data.ruling: The refutation stands. The four pin assignments in the figure are correct: GPIO 8 SPI1_RX, GPIO 10 SPI1_SCLK, GPIO 11 SPI1_TX, and GPIO 15 as the cell monitor CS (SIO, pulled up). The second clause fails. It says the isolator's enables are tied high and take no pin. The cited lines, Pins.md:105-112, say nothing about isolator enables. No other line of Pins.md or IOBoard.md at 7e74cd442a79 says it either. The datasheets also contradict it for the rank-1 barrier, ISO7741DWR. GPIO 8 is one SPI1_RX net shared by the ADS1235 (CS GPIO 9), the MAX31856 (CS GPIO 13) and, across the barrier, the ADBMS1818 (Pins.md:105, 156-158). The ISO7741's reverse channel output, OUTD (pin 6, side 1), drives a push-pull level whenever EN1 (pin 7) is high or open. Its input is the ADBMS1818 SDO. SDO is an open-drain output with a pull-up, and it goes high when CSB goes high. With EN1 tied high, OUTD therefore drives SPI1_RX high continuously. That fights the MISO output of the ADS1235 or MAX31856 whenever either is selected. To put OUTD in high impedance, EN1 must follow the cell monitor's chip select. EN1 is active high and CS is active low, so this needs an inverter from GPIO 15 or one more GPIO. Either way the figure P5 would budget (enables tied high, no part, no pin) is wrong. Scope is function: the defect concerns this barrier's connection to the shared SPI1 and the resources P5 budgets for it. It does not concern the ISO7741DWR's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity. The verifier said no page states a tri-state requirement. That does not save the clause: the figure asserts a connection that the shared net in Pins.md and the ISO7741 datasheet show to be faulty.
data.evidence:
Pins.md (checkout 7e74cd442a79), read 2026-10-03T12:00Z:
- :105 "8 | SPI1_RX | measurement SPI RX (MISO); reaches the cell monitor only across the barrier".
- :106 GPIO 9 is the ADS1235 CS; :110 GPIO 13 is the MAX31856 CS; :112 GPIO 15 is the cell monitor CS "to the host side of the isoSPI or digital-isolator barrier (V189), SIO, pulled up".
- :156-158 "The measurement coprocessor's SPI1 carries parts in different SPI modes: the ADS1235 in mode 1, the MAX31856 in mode 1 and the ADBMS1818 in mode 3".
- :173-176 says only "GPIO 15 and the SPI1 lines drive the barrier's host side". No line mentions EN1, EN2 or a tied-high enable.

ISO7741 datasheet SLLSEP4K (revised August 2026):
- Table 4-1, p. 5: EN1 is pin 7 (ISO7741). "Output pins on side 1 are enabled when EN1 is high or open and in high-impedance state when EN1 is low." On the ISO7741, IND is pin 11 (side 2) and OUTD is pin 6 (side 1).
- Table 7-2, p. 29: with EN "H or open", the output follows the input. An open input gives default High (non-F part). The output is Z only when EN is low.
- Section 5.12: VOH = VCCO - 0.2 V at -1 mA, a driven CMOS output.

ADBMS1818 Rev. B:
- Pin description: "Serial data out (SDO) is an open drain NMOS output pin. SDO requires a 5 kOhm pull-up resistor."
- Polling section: "SDO also goes high when CSB goes high".

Rank 1 of the barrier function in this run's re-rank is ISO7741DWR (scratch FU-2J/rerank-R9/final.json).
